entries.title: Spectral sufficient condition: include the Cayley degree
entries.statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on a Cayley graph from a finite symmetric generating set S of size D, let rho be the operator norm of the normalized simple random walk. The published spectral sufficient hypothesis is D*rho*p_c<1, which implies p_c<p_u. Writing p_c<1/rho omits D; when rho<1 and p_c<=1 it is automatic and cannot establish nonuniqueness. The criterion is sufficient, not necessary.
assumptions: finite symmetric simple generating set S

entries.title: Triangle-block Cayley graph defeats the universal spectral bridge
entries.statement: Let G=Cay(C_2*C_3,{a,b,b^{-1}}), where a^2=b^3=1, with iid Bernoulli bond percolation. Its degree is 3, p_c=q is the unique root in (0,1) of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1, p_u=1, and its normalized random-walk spectral radius rho obeys 3*rho*q>=2q>1.26. Thus this nonamenable Cayley graph satisfies p_c<p_u although the spectral sufficient condition D*rho*p_c<1 fails. This refutes universality or necessity of that auxiliary condition, not the Benjamini-Schramm conjecture.
entries.proof_text: The b-edges form disjoint triangles joined by a-edge bridges; contracting triangles gives a 3-regular tree. Enter a triangle through one open bridge and let K count its other vertices connected to the entry by open internal edges. Direct three-edge enumeration gives E[K]=2(p+p^2-p^3). Each such vertex has one independent fresh outward bridge, so the independent offspring mean is 2p^2+2p^3-2p^4. This is strictly increasing, crosses 1 once at q, and critical extinction holds. For q<p<1, independent closed bridges isolate infinitely many surviving off-ray branch clusters, while p=1 gives one cluster; hence p_u=1. Substitution gives q>0.63. The indicator of a single triangle has adjacency Rayleigh quotient 2, so 3*rho=||A||>=2 and 3*rho*q>1.26.
assumptions: group C_2*C_3 with the displayed simple symmetric generators
rho is normalized l2 random-walk norm

relations.rationale: The triangle-block graph has p_c<p_u while violating D*rho*p_c<1, showing the cited sufficient hypothesis is not necessary.
